previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a homeless man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and alcohol use disorder, was admitted for hypoxia, chest pain, and hemoptysis. He had received 3 liters of IV fluids in the emergency department, which led to acute pulmonary edema and worsening hypoxia. He was treated with intravenous Lasix, which improved his respiratory status and allowed him to return to room air. His chest pain was determined to be non-cardiac, with no evidence of acute ischemia or recurrent pulmonary embolism; imaging showed resolving PE and new multifocal bronchopneumonia, not requiring antibiotics. His alcohol withdrawal was managed with a short course of benzodiazepines, and he remained compliant with Lovenox. He was discharged home with stable vital signs, instructions to monitor weight, continue heart failure and anticoagulation therapy, and follow up for alcohol detox support and bilirubin monitoring.
